items.summary: fix(process): trust redacted Darwin argv only for entitled system images (#195283) * fix(process): classify redacted Darwin argument images by kernel image macOS redacts the argument image of binaries entitled with com.apple.private.no-read-procargs (mdworker), which then fails the argv alignment check as layout-mismatch. The runtime census treated that PID as unknown, so doctor --fix kept every retained updater runtime on affected Macs. Read the kernel accounting name instead: a non-JS, non-OpenClaw image is not custody doubt, matching the Windows rule. Refs #191944 * fix(process): trust only entitled system images with redacted argv layout-mismatch also fires for valid argv containing non-UTF-8 bytes, so an image name alone cannot rule out custody: a shell whose arguments point into a retained runtime would be exempted. Read the running image from its kernel text vnode and exempt it only when it is a sealed /System binary carrying com.apple.private.no-read-procargs, as mdworker does. Refs #191944 * fix(process): read the default codesign entitlement dump Some macOS 27 hosts reject the XML entitlement form for mdworker's blob, which left the intended binary unknown. Read the default key/value dump and accept either representation with an explicit true value. Refs #191944 * fix(process): confirm the Darwin image with its kernel accounting name The first lsof text mapping is ordered by address, so a process that maps an entitled binary below its own image could pose as it. Require the kernel accounting name to match that image's basename before trusting it. Refs #191944

items.title: fix(memory): adding one agent sweeps every agent database at once (#1…
items.summary: fix(memory): adding one agent sweeps every agent database at once (#195290) * fix(memory): reloading standing-intent maintenance sweeps every agent database at once Any agents.* change reloads the memory-core-standing-intents service. Start scheduled a sweep at now for every agent, so adding one agent opened every agent database together (about 470 on the reporting gateway, minutes of CPU and main-thread stalls). Deadlines learned from completed operations now live in the process-wide maintenance owner and survive the reload; only databases without a known deadline are swept immediately, and a past deadline still runs at once. Sweeps are also bounded to two at a time so first starts no longer open every store in the same instant. Refs #195272 * fix(memory): keep the match fast path off until a sweep learns absence after reload An operation in flight across a reload updates the previous owner's facts, so seeding the new owner as empty could hide an intent it just created. * fix(memory): forget a learned standing-intent deadline after an uncertain write A worker that commits and then fails leaves the cached deadline stale, so a later reload would skip the recovery sweep for that database. * fix(memory): schedule recovery when an uncertain standing-intent write invalidates its deadline A successor that inherited the old deadline during an overlapping reload would otherwise never learn the write may have committed. * fix(memory): keep the standing-intent retry backoff on repeated failed writes * test: allocate the standing-intent reload regression lines * test: correct the allocated line count to the branch delta Co-authored-by: Peter Steinberger
